text:

We have an accused, we have a suspect, we have a person accused of bribery. Firstly, bribery, which involves European funds. And unfortunately, with this majority, the Parliament, with the participation of the PPE, is blocking the lifting of the immunity of the current MP Wojciech Król.

Ladies and Gentlemen, I am appealing from this place to my colleagues from the PPE, my fellow MPs from the Platform and the PSL, to persuade them not to torpedo the activities of the European Public Prosecutor's Office, because it is a scandal and reflects poorly on us. I know this is being talked about here in the halls of the European Parliament. Subject this man to criminal liability, because what he is accused of is monstrous, and we, as Poland, would like to be cleared of it. Not everyone in Poland defends Mr. King, not everyone is in favor of covering up his suspicious dealings. We want him to be held accountable. We want him to stand trial. Persuade your colleagues and colleagues from the PPE not to block the responsibility and activities of the European Public Prosecutor's Office.

speaker: Daniel Buda
text:
Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, într-un moment de - aș putea spune - imaturitate politică profundă, domnul Grindeanu s-a gândit să dărâme guvernul condus de Ilie Bolojan, împreună cu partenerii domniei sale, de la AUR. Astăzi, domnia sa plânge în lacrimi după stabilitatea României. Mai mult, încearcă să arunce această responsabilitate în partea PNL, uitând că, în democrațiile autentice, cei care dărâmă un guvern au responsabilitatea să pună altul în loc.

Problema dumneavoastră, domnule Grindeanu, este că domnul George Simion a jucat mai bine și v-a lăsat în offside - exact așa cum PSD îi lasă pe români în offside de ani de zile, cu un deficit bugetar imens, de care însă nu v-a păsat. PNL, împreună cu USR și UDMR este aici să continuăm ceea ce am început - reformele. Ne asumăm formarea unui guvern condus de Siegfried Mureșan, un om responsabil, competent, cu experiență europeană și credibilitate.

Acum mingea este la dumneavoastră, domnule Grindeanu. Așteptăm să vedem dacă PSD vrea cu adevărat un guvern sau dacă preferă să continue spectacolul. România are nevoie de o guvernare responsabilă, nu de lecții de stabilitate din partea celor care au provocat haosul.

translation.englishText:

speaker: Victor Negrescu
text:
Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, summitul NATO de la Ankara poate schimba direcția securității europene. Pentru România, miza este uriașă, fiind pe flancul estic, la Marea Neagră. Suntem în prima linie atunci când vine vorba de securitatea euroatlantică.

Tocmai de aceea, România trebuie să fructifice această oportunitate și acest lucru reprezintă un motiv în plus pentru a avea un nou guvern care își înțelege misiunea și știe ce are de făcut. Ne trebuie investiții inteligente în apărare și în industria românească, trebuie să atragem mai multe granturi europene pentru securitate, trebuie să transformăm Marea Neagră într-o prioritate strategică în UE și NATO.

Insistențele mele pentru crearea hub-ului european de securitate maritimă la Marea Neagră prind contur. Trebuie acum să avem mai multă voință politică pentru a trece de la teorie la practică - și, din nou, un alt motiv pentru care avem nevoie de un nou guvern.

În astfel de momente, interesele României trebuie să fie mai presus de calculele politice și de aceea nu cred că trebuie să exportăm dezbaterile interne aici, în Parlamentul European. Securitatea nu așteptă, iar România trebuie să fie pregătită să își asume un rol mai important în Europa și în Alianța Nord-Atlantică.

translation.englishText:

That is precisely why Romania must take advantage of this opportunity and this is an additional reason to have a new government that understands its mission and knows what it has to do. We need smart investments in defense and Romanian industry, we need to attract more European grants for security, we need to turn the Black Sea into a strategic priority in the EU and NATO.

My insistence on the creation of the European Black Sea Maritime Security Hub is taking shape. We now need more political will to move from theory to practice - and, again, another reason why we need a new government.

In moments like these, Romania's interests must be above political calculations and that's why I don't think we should export the internal debates here, in the European Parliament. Security does not wait, and Romania must be prepared to assume a more important role in Europe and the North Atlantic Alliance.

speaker: Margarita de la Pisa Carrión
text:
Señor presidente, señorías, hoy los llamados valores europeos se utilizan como arma arrojadiza contra quienes piensan de forma diferente al discurso dominante en esta Cámara.

Lo vemos cuando se condicionan los presupuestos de la Unión Europea a criterios ideológicos como clima o género, o cuando se invocan estos mismos valores para cuestionar la legitimidad de partidos elegidos democráticamente, ignorando así la voz de millones de ciudadanos. Es una interpretación completamente desvirtuada de los valores sobre los que se fundó este proyecto de paz y que hoy solo genera polarización y enfrentamiento.

Los verdaderos valores europeos —como la dignidad de la persona, la igualdad y la libertad— hoy se pretenden sustituir por conceptos que ni siquiera formaban parte de los fundamentos de la Unión, que quieren romper con el orden natural y que acaban con la riqueza que cada uno de nosotros puede aportar.

Dejen de excluir a quienes estamos preocupados por las dificultades que supone hoy emprender una familia o cualquier otro proyecto, por los crecientes problemas de seguridad o el incremento de la pobreza. No se apropien de los valores europeos.

Stop excluding those of us who are concerned about the difficulties of starting a family or any other project today, due to the growing security problems or the increase in poverty. Do not appropriate European values.

speaker: Emma Wiesner
text:
Mr President, it is 'Pride Month', and I'm getting seriously tired with the LGBT+ minority. You are demanding, loud, unhappy, feeling sorry for yourself. I am normally very supportive of minorities, but with you guys, I'm having some serious issues.

Because at some point you need to understand that love is love. And don't let your hate out on the trans, the drag, the gay, and the queer community.

I am also tired of the statement that we should 'celebrate the minority'. The queer community – we are not the ones in the minority. 69 % of Europeans want the same rights for the LGBTQ+ community. 72 % of Europeans support same-sex marriage and 64 % believe in trans rights.

The minority here are the ones spreading fear and hate, and it's not them that we should celebrate. We are in the majority and every month should be a pride month.

speaker: Jaume Asens Llodrà
text:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, ¿ha visto el vídeo donde aparece un ministro animando a sus soldados, entre aplausos y risas, a estrellar a bebés palestinos contra las rocas?

¿Ha leído el informe de la ONU que habla de ello? ¿De un genocidio deliberado contra la infancia palestina? La misma semana en que ustedes —la Comisión Europea— estrechaban la mano con sus responsables en Tel Aviv. Y, por eso, la derecha ha impedido que hagamos un debate sobre ese informe, porque ese informe es un acto de acusación moral y criminal contra la Europa que representan y que sigue colaborando, con sus armas y sus acuerdos, con ese infanticidio.

Cuando un bebé es asesinado, no solo se apaga una vida, se oscurece nuestro mundo entero. No hay nada más silencioso que un patio de colegio que se convierte en un cementerio, ni nada más cruel que una niña que es abatida cuando busca comida. Solo hay algo peor: la complicidad de quien arma al francotirador.

There is nothing quieter than a schoolyard that becomes a cemetery, nor anything more cruel than a girl who is shot down while looking for food. There is only one thing worse: the complicity of the person who arms the sniper.

speaker: Estrella Galán
text:
Señor presidente, Donald Trump ha llamado al presidente de la FIFA exigiendo retirar la sanción al delantero estrella de los Estados Unidos. La FIFA ha pasado por el aro y esta noche el jugador saldrá al campo contra Bélgica. El mundo entero ha visto cómo unos pocos poderosos se saltan impunemente las reglas del fútbol y, además, presumen de ello.

Eso que hoy soporta en un campo de fútbol un equipo concreto, lo llevan soportando los ciudadanos y ciudadanas saharauis en los campos de refugiados desde hace mucho tiempo. Y, además, esto es mucho más grave —desde hace 50 años—, porque siguen viendo cómo unos pocos se saltan las reglas del Derecho internacional. Lo hace Marruecos con la ocupación militar y negando el referéndum saharaui. Lo hace la Unión Europea negando la sentencia del Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea. Y lo hace España, no cumpliendo sus obligaciones con la que fue su provincia n.º 53 y también excluyendo del proceso de regularización a este colectivo. Por eso, la proposición de ley que está propuesta en estos momentos sobre la mesa para reconocer la nacionalidad salda parte de la deuda con el pueblo saharaui.

No lo olvidemos, es un paso fundamental, pero no un sustituto del derecho de autodeterminación que vamos a exigir hasta el final.

FIFA has jumped through the hoops and tonight the player will take the field against Belgium. The whole world has seen how a few powerful people break the rules of football with impunity and, furthermore, boast about it.

What a specific team endures today on a soccer field has been endured by Sahrawi citizens in refugee camps for a long time. And, furthermore, this is much more serious - for 50 years - because they continue to see how a few break the rules of international law. Morocco does it with the military occupation and denying the Sahrawi referendum. The European Union does so by denying the ruling of the Court of Justice of the European Union. And Spain does it, not fulfilling its obligations with what was its 53rd province and also excluding this group from the regularization process. For this reason, the bill that is currently proposed on the table to recognize nationality settles part of the debt with the Sahrawi people.

Let us not forget, it is a fundamental step, but not a substitute for the right of self-determination that we will demand until the end.

speaker: Alexander Jungbluth
text:
Herr Präsident! Was wir am Rande des AfD‑Parteitags in Erfurt erleben mussten, war ein beispielloser, brutaler Angriff auf die Pressefreiheit in Deutschland. Journalisten von Apollo News wurden von einem linken Mob durch die Straßen gejagt, verprügelt und krankenhausreif getreten. Auf der Pressekonferenz des linksextremen Bündnisses widersetzen wird diese Gewalt legitimiert. O‑Ton der Linksextremisten: Faschisten mit Presseausweis sind immer noch Faschisten. Wer nicht stramm links berichtet, wird für vogelfrei erklärt und auf offener Straße gelyncht.

Und die linke Elite in Deutschland? Sie klatscht Beifall. Die AfD und die Presse sind dabei nicht die einzigen Feinde; offen droht das linksextreme widersetzen auch der CDU und damit der EVP. Lassen Sie uns also abermals rechte Mehrheiten im Parlament schaffen, um die Pressefreiheit vor den Kommunisten und Linken zu schützen.

speaker: Fernand Kartheiser
text:
Mr President, the case of Finnish MP Päivi Räsänen should alarm us. Finland's Supreme Court convicted her for expressing Christian beliefs on marriage in a church pamphlet written over 20 years ago. The implications go far beyond Finland.

Under the EU's Digital Services Act (the DSA), online platforms must remove so-called hate speech. If a national court decides that a Bible-based quote constitutes hate speech, platforms across the entire EU are compelled to remove it. Every Member State must comply, regardless of its own constitutional order and guarantees. We cannot allow a single national ruling to override the fundamental rights of 450 million people. Freedom of speech and freedom of religion are among the very foundations of our democratic order. We therefore need urgent changes and to repeal the DSA to ensure that it can no longer be weaponised to suppress these fundamental rights.

speaker: Günther Sidl
text: Herr Präsident! Das EU‑Parlament kann auch diese Woche zeigen, dass es ein wichtiger Motor für den Umweltschutz ist, wenn wir über Anpassungen im Umweltstrafrecht und über Themen wie die Wasserresilienz reden. Gleichzeitig dürfen wir aber nie die Grundlagen für eine gesunde Umwelt und einen intakten Wasserkreislauf aus den Augen verlieren, nämlich gesunde Böden und Gewässer und ihre Gefährdung durch Pestizide. Sorgen wir endlich für einen ganzheitlichen Ansatz, der für mehr Ertragssicherheit in der Landwirtschaft und weniger Belastung unserer natürlichen Ressourcen sorgt! Wir brauchen wirksame und ökologische Pestizidalternativen, und dafür brauchen wir eine europäische Forschungsinitiative, die auch in der Gemeinsamen Agrarpolitik fest verankert sein muss. De ani de zile, multe atlete au fost private de victorii, medalii și burse din cauza acestei practici aberante promovate de stânga neomarxistă. Vă puteți imagina o competiție sportivă de box în care un bărbat care se pretinde femeie boxează cu o femeie biologică? Vă puteți imagina o competiție sportivă în care nu mai avem categorii de greutate - și dacă cineva care e mai solid se identifică ca o persoană mai slabă, să boxeze la o categorie net inferioară?

E timpul ca și Europa să se trezească. Respectați drepturile femeilor, recunoscând faptul că un bărbat biologic e diferit de o femeie biologică - și respectăm această realitate biologică.

It's time for Europe to wake up too. Respect women's rights by recognizing that a biological male is different from a biological female - and we respect this biological reality.

speaker: Helmut Brandstätter
text:

Da gibt es einen Art Journalisten in der Schweiz – ich glaube, Köppel heißt er –, der sagt: Nein, der Putin ist eh lieb. Nein, er bedroht auch die Schweiz, und selbstverständlich bedroht er auch uns. Und was auch gesagt wird: Es gibt ja Sanktionen, aber die werden umgangen, und da muss sich die EU deutlicher darum kümmern.

Jetzt gibt es eine sozialdemokratische Abgeordnete in der Schweiz, die sagt, die Schweiz brauche eine engere Anbindung an EU und NATO; wer glaubt, die Schweiz könne sich im Ernstfall allein schützen, der irrt.

Und das heißt wohl, dass wir uns nur gemeinsam verteidigen können hier in Europa, und dazu rufe ich alle auf – natürlich auch meine Freunde in der österreichischen Heimat.

And that probably means that we can only defend ourselves together here in Europe, and I call on everyone to do so - including, of course, my friends in my Austrian homeland.

Vreau să vă atrag atenția. Este un viitor catastrofal dacă nu ne ocupăm de viitorul joburilor tinerilor Europei și României.

translation.englishText:

And those who have jobs will do the work of three people, because that's what the companies say: "Now we've given you AI, so you can work even more for the same money, with the same power."

I want to draw your attention. It is a catastrophic future if we do not deal with the future of jobs for the young people of Europe and Romania.

text:
Herr Präsident! Aber Propaganda, wissen wir auch, das ist etwas, was man technologisch voranbringen kann, und deswegen waren viele Menschen so erschüttert und entsetzt, als sie von Recherchen hörten, dass die AfD jetzt ein KI‑System nutzt, ein KI‑System, in dem Nachrichten nach Empörungspotenzial bewertet werden und da ein Post für Social Media erstellt wird – automatisiert. Das ist Propaganda auf Knopfdruck.

Wir haben zu Recht im AI Act gesagt: Hochrisiko‑KI‑Systeme, die Wahlen beeinflussen sollen, die müssen als solches gekennzeichnet werden, die müssen auch untersagt werden. Deswegen bitte ich die Kommission, dass sie sich das genau anguckt. Ich appelliere an uns, dass wir unsere eigenen Regeln zum Schutz vor KI‑Propaganda nicht noch weiter in die Zukunft schieben, denn das macht den Menschen zu Recht auch Sorge.
topic: One-minute speeches on matters of political importance

translation.englishText:

But propaganda, we also know, is something that can be advanced technologically, and that's why many people were so shocked and horrified when they heard about research that the AfD is now using an AI system, an AI system in which news is rated according to its outrage potential and a post for social media is created - automatically. This is propaganda at the push of a button.

We rightly said in the AI ​​Act: High-risk AI systems that are intended to influence elections must be labeled as such and must also be prohibited. That's why I ask the Commission to take a close look at this. I appeal to us not to push our own rules for protection against AI propaganda further into the future, because that rightly worries people.

text:

translation.englishText:

A modern car is not just a car, it is a computer on wheels. It knows exactly where you've been driving, it collects data and it's always connected. This is not only climate policy, this is industrial policy, but it is also security policy.

Climate policy must never become a security policy goal in itself.

speaker: Barry Cowen
text:
Mr President, colleagues, hundreds of thousands of car manufacturers leaving Europe. Thousands more jobs in agritech, steel and chemical sectors. We hear stories like these almost every day and we're often told who's to blame: it's China, it's South America, it's unfair competition, it's illegal state subsidies.

And yes, sometimes factors like market distortions and unfair trade practices play a role, but there is a saying back home: before pointing the finger at someone else, make sure your own house is in order.

Our energy costs remain among the highest in the developed world. Planning and permitting take far too long. We talk endlessly about strategic autonomy, yet still, we have to move heaven and earth to build infrastructure the likes of a European supergrid. Trade defences have their place, but Europe's biggest competitiveness problem is Europe itself.

So, when the EU Commission holds trade talks with the likes of China, many spend their time calling for more tariffs and bans. But I know what we should remain focused on: making Europe competitive again. We need to permit quicker, invest more, build faster and lower costs because the best way to protect European jobs isn't keeping others out. It's making Europe competitive again.

speaker: Reinier Van Lanschot
text:
Mr President, Rutte said it clearly: Russia is not afraid of commitments but of capabilities. But the conversation about Europe's safety is stranded at money, percentages. We never even touched on capabilities, even when the US withdraws bombers, withdraws tankers and withdraws troops.

We need a European defence union, but our national leaders can't seem to see beyond their nationalistic noses. That is why 30 Members of the European Parliament – from The Left to the EPP, from Spain to Finland – call on them: at least do the most obvious thing first. Decide at the NATO summit to buy, maintain and operate the most critical capabilities together, as Europe. NATO will become stronger with two pillars – one American, one European; separable, but not separate.

Let's not wait for war to unite us. Let's unite to prevent war.

speaker: Sandra Gómez López
text:
Señor presidente, como valenciana, tengo que empezar lamentando el incendio que hemos sufrido en Soneja, en Castellón, que ha arrasado más de 183 hectáreas y, por suerte, no ha habido víctimas, pero no podemos ignorar lo que nos dice este incendio.

Las sequías y las olas de calor nos llevan a unas consecuencias del cambio climático que no son una amenaza de futuro: tienen consecuencias en el presente, de dolor y de sufrimiento. Y tenemos que actuar ya.

Pasando al punto por el que quería preguntar, ¿cuántas horas ha pasado este Pleno debatiendo sobre los Gobiernos de Venezuela, sobre Maduro o Delcy Rodríguez? Y ahora que su pueblo más nos necesita, ¿qué nos pasa? ¿Nos hemos quedado mudos? ¿Por qué no exigimos que Estados Unidos asuma su responsabilidad con Venezuela?

Hace poco Trump presumía de todo el dinero que estaban ganando gracias al petróleo de Venezuela. Pues cada céntimo de ese petróleo venezolano tiene que ir a recuperar al pueblo y a recuperar a la población civil venezolana, que está pasando por uno de los peores momentos de su historia. Venezuela no se va a reconstruir en los 48 minutos que presumía Trump que le costó ganar la guerra en Venezuela. Es por eso por lo que debemos exigir que cada céntimo sea para ellos.

Pasando al punto por el que quería preguntar, ¿cuántas horas ha pasado este Pleno debatiendo sobre los Gobiernos de Venezuela, sobre Maduro o Delcy Rodríguez? Hace poco Trump presumía de todo el dinero que estaban ganando gracias al petróleo de Venezuela. Pues cada céntimo de ese petróleo venezolano tiene que ir a recuperar al pueblo y a recuperar a la población civil venezolana, que está pasando por uno de los peores momentos de su historia. Venezuela no se va a reconstruir en los 48 minutos que presumía Trump que le costó ganar la guerra en Venezuela. Es por eso por lo que debemos exigir que cada céntimo sea para ellos.

speaker: Marie Dauchy
text:
Monsieur le Président, l’Union européenne promettait de protéger notre industrie: elle organise aujourd’hui son déclin. En France, et particulièrement dans mon département, la Savoie, les conséquences sont bien réelles. Vous avez contribué à la fermeture de la cartonnerie DS Smith avec des réglementations toujours plus absurdes. Pendant que vous imposez des contraintes à nos entreprises, vous laissez la concurrence chinoise déloyale frapper de plein fouet des fleurons industriels comme Ferroglobe.

Et maintenant, vous voulez interdire les PFAS, une molécule utilisée partout dans l’industrie, jusque dans nos poêles Tefal. Dans ce sigle, il y a des usines, des salariés et des familles. Si une substance est dangereuse, oui, elle doit être interdite. Mais vous choisissez une interdiction globale qui met dans le même sac plus de 10 000 molécules, alors même que celle utilisée par Tefal, par exemple, est scientifiquement reconnue comme stable, non toxique et sans danger sur la santé.

À force de tout vouloir interdire, vous nous empêchez de produire. L’Europe n’a pas besoin d’une nouvelle interdiction: elle a besoin d’une politique qui protège enfin son industrie. Après le nucléaire et l’automobile, refusez au moins de faire des PFAS le prochain cimetière de l’industrie française.
topic: One-minute speeches on matters of political importance

By wanting to ban everything, you prevent us from producing. Europe does not need a new ban: it needs a policy that finally protects its industry. After nuclear power and automobiles, at least refuse to make PFAS the next graveyard of French industry.

speaker: Ciaran Mullooly
text:
Mr President, the COVID‑19 pandemic is over, but the scars remain. This week, I met with Care Champions, an independent Irish advocacy organisation representing people who were affected both in the community and in care homes.

I met Angela Moore, who lost both her parents within 13 weeks of each other. The staff who were looking after them could no longer enter her house because of a public health policy. Anne Gallagher tried to book a visit to see her husband in a nursing home on the 19 December, but was not allowed. Her husband Brendan passed away later that day. Majella Beattie's mother, Mary Jane, was told if she deteriorated, she could not be accommodated in an ICU due to her age and dementia.

These are real people, real relatives, real families, people who are entitled to the truth. They're entitled to their day. We need a proper public inquiry and we need it for one reason: so that we can investigate the proper safeguarding of vulnerable adults in our society.
topic: One-minute speeches on matters of political importance

speaker: Juan Fernando López Aguilar
text:
Señor presidente, comisario, el 12 de junio entraron definitivamente en vigor los ocho Reglamentos del Pacto sobre Migración y Asilo, es decir, leyes europeas vinculantes para los Estados miembros. Y, en coincidencia, dos años después de esa aprobación definitiva por el Parlamento Europeo, se ha aprobado aquí nada menos que el infame Reglamento sobre el Retorno, que camina en la dirección contraria al Pacto, porque autoriza a los Estados miembros a financiar, a través de acuerdos bilaterales, la construcción de centros de internamiento para personas irregulares enviándolas a un país tercero que no es su país de origen ni de tránsito.

Ahora bien, la vuelta de tuerca moralmente insoportable se produjo la semana pasada con ese encuentro infame de representantes del régimen de la tiranía talibán con funcionarios de la Comisión Europea. Esa tiranía talibán que oprime sistemáticamente a su población y que somete nada menos que a las mujeres, que son la mitad de la población, a un apartheid de género.

Por tanto, la pregunta es obligada: ¿cómo hemos llegado a esto? ¿Queda tiempo para corregirlo antes de la próxima moción de censura contra la Comisión?

speaker: Petra Steger
text:
Herr Präsident! Spanien will 1,3 Millionen Illegale legalisieren. Das ist kein humanitärer Akt, das ist ein sicherheitspolitischer Wahnsinn und eine gewaltige Bedrohung für ganz Europa. Das sind Millionen neue Pull-Faktoren, ein brandgefährliches Signal an die ganze Welt: Kommt nur alle illegal her, am Ende dürft ihr sowieso bleiben.

Und was macht Brüssel, was macht Kommissar Brunner? Nichts. Kein Wort der Kritik, gar nichts. Wenn Orbán Grenzen schützt, kommen hunderte Millionen Strafzahlungen. Und jetzt bei einer linken Regierung? Rechtsbruch – egal. Die EU müsste jetzt sofort handeln und migrationspolitischen Notstand ausrufen und Spanien sanktionieren. Aber warum sollte eine Kommission noch reagieren, die seit mehr als zehn Jahren tatenlos zuschaut, wie Europa zerstört wird durch diese kulturfremde Massenmigration, eine Kommission, die auch jetzt wieder ihre eindeutige ideologische Schlagseite gezeigt hat, indem sie den Save Europe Act, eine Bürgerinitiative für Remigration mit fast 500 000 Unterschriften, wegen angeblichen Verstoßes gegen EU-Werte abgedreht hat? Das ist ein riesengroßer Skandal und ein Fußtritt der Demokratie und Mitbestimmung.
topic: One-minute speeches on matters of political importance

This is a huge scandal and a step on democracy and co-determination.

text:

speaker: Michael McNamara
text:
Mr President, as Ireland assumes the presidency of the European Union, I think it begs questions about what education system is required to be European and to serve that. It seems to me that two things are essential.

The first is that we start teaching children European languages as early as possible in their education.

The other is, of course, that we maintain an education system whereby Irish people can obtain an education through the medium of the Irish language for the entirety of their education, it being our first language. There are translators in booths now translating this into Irish.

Unfortunately, neither is possible. In 2020, the Minister for Education promised that we would start teaching modern European languages in third class in primary school. That hasn't happened and instead of getting closer to happening, it's getting further away. Teachers are being left to their own devices, not receiving the training and not receiving the resources.

In Clare, where I come from, where the biggest town in my constituency is, there is no second-level education school whereby people can get a full education in the Irish language. That also needs to change.

text:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, sufinanciranje projekata u Europskoj uniji sve češće postaje zapreka razvoju, osobito na lokalnim razinama. Manje lokalne jedinice koje raspolažu sa slabim fiskalnim kapacitetom sve teže osiguravaju financijska sredstva, odnosno vlastiti udio za sufinanciranje tih projekata, pa čak i za one projekte koji su ključni za građane.

Istovremeno, imamo neujednačene kriterije, imamo politički utjecaj kod raspodjele sredstava, što je rezultat sve veće regionalne razlike. Po posljednjem izvješću Europske komisije, u Hrvatskoj glavni grad Zagreb je na 131 posto prosjeka Europske unije, dok je panonska Hrvatska samo na 52 posto prosjeka Europske unije.

Ako želimo stvarnu koheziju, onda moramo osigurati pravednije uvjete za sufinanciranje i omogućiti da one lokalne jedinice koje raspolažu s manje resursa ne budu zakinute.
topic: One-minute speeches on matters of political importance

translation.englishText:
Dear Chairman, the co-financing of projects in the European Union is increasingly becoming an obstacle to development, especially at local levels. Smaller local units with weak fiscal capacity find it increasingly difficult to secure financial resources, that is, their own share for the co-financing of these projects, and even for those projects that are crucial for citizens.

At the same time, we have uneven criteria, we have political influence in the distribution of funds, which is the result of growing regional differences. According to the latest report of the European Commission, in Croatia, the capital Zagreb is at 131 percent of the European Union average, while Pannonian Croatia is only at 52 percent of the European Union average.

If we want real cohesion, then we must ensure fairer conditions for co-financing and ensure that those local units with fewer resources are not deprived.

Herr talman! Kollegor! I dag vill jag tala om något fruktansvärt som skakat Sverige. En svensk medborgare och polis, Christian Zedig, har mördats i Köpenhamn i en brutal och meningslös våldshandling. En vanlig semesterkväll och fotbollsfirande förvandlades till en tragedi, och en familj har nu lämnats i stor sorg och saknad. En fru som har förlorat sin man och två barn som har förlorat sin pappa. Våra tankar går till dem, till andra anhöriga, kollegor och vänner.

När våld bryter in skadas tilliten i våra samhällen. I städer, på torg och evenemang runt om i Europa ska vi kunna röra oss fritt utan att känna rädsla. Respekt för lag och ordning är inte bara nationella projekt utan gemensamma europeiska värderingar.

Personer som inte har rätt att vara i Europa ska inte kunna hota vår trygghet. Ytterst handlar det om att försvara våra europeiska värderingar och vårt sätt att leva. Vila i frid.
topic: Recent violent and fatal attacks in Italy and Denmark and their implications for public security in Europe

speaker: Susanna Ceccardi
text:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, quante altre vittime serviranno, prima che l'Europa trovi il coraggio di guardare la realtà negli occhi? Quante ancora?

A Milano, un uomo di 55 anni è stato accoltellato oltre 20 volte mentre faceva colazione con il padre. L'aggressore, un giovane nato in Italia da genitori gambiani, dopo l'arresto ha dichiarato: "Mi sono divertito. Appena esco, lo rifaccio".

In Svezia, un poliziotto di 32 anni è stato assassinato da un uomo di origine africana con precedenti penali mentre guardava una partita dei Mondiali.

Sono il volto di un'Europa che per troppo tempo ha preferito voltarsi dall'altra parte.

In troppi casi, gli autori di queste violenze sono giovani nati o cresciuti in Europa, figli dell'immigrazione. La verità è che l'integrazione non si proclama, si costruisce e quando fallisce, il prezzo lo pagano i cittadini innocenti.

Per anni ci hanno detto che bastava accogliere, che tutto si sarebbe risolto da solo, che denunciare questi problemi era intolleranza. Oggi sono i fatti a smentire questa ideologia.

Ma adesso non basta più parlare solo di fermare l'immigrazione illegale, è arrivato il momento di parlare di remigrazione: l'Unione europea deve organizzare una vera politica europea di remigrazione, anche attraverso Frontex.

text:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il tema della sicurezza pubblica in Europa merita certamente la massima attenzione ed è una grande emergenza in alcune aree del mio paese – dell'Italia – in particolare per quanto riguarda la lotta alla criminalità organizzata e alle mafie, ancora forti e presenti sul territorio.

La mia regione è la Sicilia, la terra di Giovanni Falcone e di Paolo Borsellino, di tante donne e uomini che hanno dato la loro vita per combattere la mafia e affermare la legalità.

In particolare, negli ultimi mesi, la mia città – Palermo – ha registrato numerosi episodi di violenza legati al fenomeno mafioso: diversi esercizi commerciali hanno subito violenti atti intimidatori, alcuni sono stati dati alle fiamme e più volte la criminalità organizzata ha sparato con fucili d'assalto, meglio conosciuti come kalashnikov, per intimorire gli onesti imprenditori e indurli a sottomettersi alla logica mafiosa.

A qualche imprenditore è stata recentemente assegnata la scorta per ragioni di sicurezza e incolumità personali, così come recentemente accaduto ad amministratori locali, per ultimo un assessore del mio comune, Palermo.

Dinanzi a tutto ciò, la risposta del governo Meloni è stata fin qui, a mio avviso, del tutto insoddisfacente. Il ministro Piantedosi ha annunciato il rafforzamento di un sistema di videocamere, ma attendiamo misure concrete per il potenziamento degli organici delle forze dell'ordine e della magistratura, per un'efficace contrasto alla criminalità mafiosa, che estende i suoi affari criminali in tutta Europa.

Anche per questo – concludo – mi auguro che la direttiva riguardante il recupero e la confisca dei beni venga presto recepita da tutti gli Stati membri, in modo da produrre risultati efficaci, così come li ha prodotti in Italia la legge La Torre sulla confisca dei beni confiscati alla mafia.

speaker: Charlie Weimers
text:
Herr talman! Det kunde ha varit jag. En fin sommarkväll i Köpenhamn: öl, kompisar, VM på storbildsskärm – svårt att tänka mig något bättre. Det var så kvällen var tänkt för Christian Zedig. Han var 32 år, pappa till två små barn och polis. Han var ledig den dagen. Han försökte bara lugna ner ett bråk, och det var då invandrargänget gav sig på honom. Han slogs ner och stampades på huvudet gång på gång. Han dödades för att han var den som tog ansvar.

Herr talman! Samma vecka knivhuggs en oskyldig man i Milano 20 gånger av en gambiansk invandrare. Gerardo åt frukost med sin far på ett kafé och det kunde ha varit vem som helst av oss här inne. Två attacker i två länder, men samma fråga som vi inte längre kan blunda för. När sådana här saker händer gång på gång, då måste vi våga tala om det.

Ändå röstade socialdemokrater, vänstern och de gröna emot att Europaparlamentet ens skulle få hålla en debatt om de här attackerna och vad de betyder för säkerheten i Europa. Ni rödgröna vill inte ens diskutera det, och det var ni som inte ens kunde ställa er bakom återvändandeförordningen – en lag som kommer att göra det enklare att skicka hem utländska våldsverkare som begår allvarliga brott här i Europa.

Ni säger nej till att tala om problemen. Ni säger nej till att göra någonting åt det. Det här är inte ett politiskt spel, det här är på riktigt. Bakom varje attack finns en familj som aldrig mer blir densamma. Det finns barn som förlorar sin pappa. Vi är skyldiga Christian, Gerardo och alla offer mer än tomma ord. Vi är skyldiga dem handling.

speaker: Abir Al-Sahlani
text:
Herr talman! Fotbolls-VM ska vara en folkfest, en plats för glädje, gemenskap och hopp. Istället reste en svensk fotbollssupporter för att uppleva fotboll och kom aldrig hem. Till Christians familj och vänner vill jag uttrycka min djupaste sorg och mitt varmaste deltagande. Må ni finna tröst och ljus i denna bottenlösa sorg.

När ett sådant här fruktansvärt brott sker väcks ilska, sorg och rädsla. Det är bara mänskligt, men det är just i sådana fall och stunder som rättsstaten prövas. Vi som politiker är inte domarna. Vi är inte åklagarna, och vi är inte de som avgör skuld eller straff. Vi är lagstiftare. Vårt ansvar är att se till att människor kan leva i trygghet, att ge polis och rättsväsende de verktyg som behövs för att förebygga, utreda och lagföra dem som begår brotten, och att försvara rättsstaten även när känslorna är som starkast.

Det är därför det är så anmärkningsvärt att Charlie Weimers från Sverigedemokraterna ännu en gång väljer att använda en enskild människas tragiska död för att vinna politiska poänger. När ett pågående brottsfall blir ett politiskt slagträ flyttas fokus från offret och blir retorisk rekvisita. Christian förtjänar bättre. Hans familj förtjänar bättre och den här kammaren förtjänar bättre.

Den här kammaren kan mer än den här nivån. Låt rättsväsendet göra sitt arbete. Låt oss hedra Christian med respekt och inte använda hans minne som politisk rekvisita. Låt oss vara de lagstiftare som våra medborgare förväntar sig att vi ska vara: principfasta, ansvarstagande och värdiga det förtroende de har gett oss.

translation.englishText:
Mr Speaker! The World Cup should be a public celebration, a place for joy, community and hope. Instead, a Swedish football supporter traveled to experience football and never came home. To Christian's family and friends, I want to express my deepest sorrow and my warmest sympathy. May you find comfort and light in this bottomless sorrow.

When a terrible crime like this happens, anger, sadness and fear are aroused. It is only human, but it is precisely in such cases and moments that the rule of law is tested. We as politicians are not the judges. We are not the prosecutors, and we are not the ones to determine guilt or punishment. We are legislators. Our responsibility is to ensure that people can live in safety, to give the police and justice system the tools they need to prevent, investigate and prosecute those who commit the crimes, and to defend the rule of law even when emotions are at their strongest.

That is why it is so remarkable that Charlie Weimers of the Sweden Democrats once again chooses to use the tragic death of an individual to score political points. When an ongoing criminal case becomes a political bat, the focus shifts from the victim and becomes a rhetorical prop. Christian deserves better. His family deserves better and this House deserves better.

This chamber is capable of more than this level. Let the judiciary do its job. Let's honor Christian with respect and not use his memory as a political prop. Let us be the legislators our citizens expect us to be: principled, accountable and worthy of the trust they have placed in us.

speaker: Alexander Sell
text:
Herr Präsident! 80 Messerstechereien am Tag, über 1 000 Tote im Jahr – das ist die Situation in Deutschland. Wir reden aber heute über Italien und Dänemark. Über Deutschland reden wir gar nicht mehr, weil wir uns an die Gewalt gewöhnt haben. Solingen, Mannheim, Aschaffenburg, Polizisten, Zugbegleiter, Kinder – überall in Deutschland werden unschuldige Menschen Opfer sinnloser Gewalt. Aber nicht nur Messer kommen dabei zum Einsatz, sondern immer öfter auch Schusswaffen; jeden Tag gibt es Schießereien in Berlin. In Stade in Niedersachsen wurden vor einer Woche sechs Menschen erschossen, in einem Mutter‑Kind‑Heim – kaltblütig ermordet, weil sie einem Kind helfen wollten.

Wer sind die Täter? Auch hier ist die polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik eindeutig: Bei schweren Gewaltdelikten sind Syrer und Afghanen zehnmal häufiger Tatverdächtige als Deutsche. Kriminelle syrische Clans machen sich in Dortmund, Bremen oder Berlin breit mit massiver Gewalt.

Ich frage Sie: Wie kann es sein, dass Menschen, die angeblich vor einem Krieg geflüchtet sind, bei uns kriminell werden? Wie kann es sein, dass Menschen, die von uns alles bekommen – Wohnung, Bürgergeld, Krankenversicherung; über die Hälfte der Syrer lebt in Deutschland vom Bürgergeld –, wie kann es sein, dass diese Menschen bei uns morden, rauben und vergewaltigen?

Weil sie eine andere Kultur haben. Weil sie unsere Großzügigkeit für Schwäche halten, und weil sie ihre Familienehre über unser Recht und unser Gesetz stellen.

Es gibt deshalb nur eine Antwort auf die eskalierende Gewalt: Remigration. Wir müssen diese Leute in ihre Heimat zurückbringen. Wer angegriffen wird, muss sich verteidigen.

That is the difference between a tough political debate and racist abuse, and that is what we cannot tolerate in this House. That's why I ask you and the Presidium - can you please keep your mouth shut when I'm talking, Mr. Jungbluth? That's why I ask you to confront this, to examine it, because despite all the justified concern, despite all the justified anger, there can be no room for racism in this House because people are being murdered.

Herr Präsident! Ich war mir fast sicher, dass es dazu kommen würde, Herr Sell; ich hätte wirklich ein Monatsgehalt darauf gewettet.

Herr Präsident, ich möchte mich zur Ausführung der rechtlichen Analyse, warum das hier ein Verstoß gegen Artikel 10 Absatz 3 und Artikel 10 Absatz 4 der Geschäftsordnung ist, des Rechtsvergleichs bedienen. Der Kollege Weimers, der hat Sachen gesagt, denen ich vielleicht nicht in allem folgen kann, die sich aber im Rahmen einer respektvollen Auseinandersetzung bewegen. Der Kollege Sell hat gesagt, dass diese Menschen rauben, morden und vergewaltigen, weil sie eine andere Kultur haben. Das war die Aussage.

Das ist der Unterschied zwischen einer harten politischen Auseinandersetzung und rassistischen Ausfällen, und das ist das, was wir hier in diesem Haus nicht tolerieren können. Deswegen bitte ich Sie und das Präsidium – können Sie mal bitte den Mund halten, wenn ich rede, Herr Jungbluth? Deswegen bitte ich Sie, dem entgegenzutreten, das zu prüfen, denn bei aller berechtigten Sorge, bei aller berechtigten Wut kann in diesem Haus nicht, weil Menschen ermordet werden, Platz für Rassismus sein.
